written: 2026-10-20, before any v3 model was trained or scored and before any detector (v1, v2 or v3) was scored on the fresh test windows
purpose: Detector v3 (CPU only): more trustworthy test numbers and better tiny-smoke and clear-scene behaviour, from a fresh, larger test set, box labels for the dev smoke windows and background hard negatives.

fresh_test.figlib_test2: 79 FIgLib sequences on the test camera mounts that no earlier set used (two windows before and two after the first visible plume each; 308 windows from 77 sequences, 157 smoke, 18 cameras); labels from the library's ignition times, as for the FIgLib set
fresh_test.hpwren_bg_test: one daytime window per camera-day (08-17 local) on 21 archived test cameras, 2026-07 to 2026-10, on days without a CAL FIRE incident within 70 km in the previous 7 days or the next day (234 downloaded); labels: blind AI smoke and fog votes (configs/real/hpwren_background_labeling_guide.md; two votes per sheet, a third where they disagree or one is unsure); windows labelled smoke unknown or of bad quality are left out
fresh_test.status: never scored by any detector before the v3 candidate is frozen; scored once, v1, v2 and v3 side by side (scripts/score_detector.py)

dev_additions.hpwren_bg: the same kind of background windows on dev cameras (5 per camera; corrected: selected, like the test windows, on days without a CAL FIRE incident within 70 km in the previous 7 days or the next day, 2026-08-01 to 2026-10-18, seed v3dev, cameras of the earlier HPWREN sets only; this entry first said 100 km / 14 days, which was not what had been run), labelled the same way, as hard negatives
dev_additions.boxes: configs/real/smoke_dev_boxes.csv: AI boxes around the plume on the 653 dev smoke windows (minutes 0, 4, 8, 11); the tile and zoom heads are fitted on tile labels from the minute-11 box (scripts/box_labels.py, src/detector/boxes.py)

dev_selection: dev cameras only (camera-mount grouped 5-fold CV). Variants compared: (a) v2's recipe on the dev sets plus hpwren_bg; (b) (a) with box-supervised tile and zoom heads; (c) (b) with balanced positive / negative tile weights; (d) the best of (b, c) plus the reference tile head. The criterion is the dev out-of-fold within-set smoke AUROC; a variant whose dev false alarms on all smoke-free windows at the deploy point are higher than (a)'s by more than 1 point is not chosen. Operating rules as v2 (deploy: 80 % dev recall, never above 2.5 % dev fog alarms; strict: 5 % of dev smoke-free windows; fog veto 0.95; stack fog weight 3). The chosen variant and its dev numbers are added below as a revision before the fresh test is scored.

primary_fresh_test.figlib_test2_smoke_auroc: >= 0.78 (tiny early smoke; v1 on the old test: 0.713)
primary_fresh_test.hpwren_bg_test_false_alarms_deploy: <= 15 % of the smoke-free background windows alarm at the deploy point (clear scenes on ordinary days)

secondary_old_test.note: the old test cameras (440 windows) were scored by v1 and v2 already, so these checks are not blind
secondary_old_test.fire_day_smoke_auroc: hpwren_smoke and hpwren_smoke2 each not lower than v1 by more than 0.02

targets_7_of_10.verdict: 7/10 if both primary targets and all secondary checks are met; the paired v3 - v1 differences on the fresh test (camera bootstrap) are reported whether or not they exclude zero

caveats: AI labels on the background windows and AI boxes are not human-checked; FIgLib labels come from the ignition time, so a window right after ignition can show no smoke yet; 18-21 test cameras make camera-level intervals wide
revisions: 2026-10-20, after dev cross-validation and before any v3 model was scored on any test camera, chosen variant: (d) box-supervised tile and zoom heads (boxes of every confidence: 'low' and 'medium' minimum compared on dev, low equal or better), without positive/negative balancing ((c) tied (b) on dev within-set AUROC, 0.855 both, so the simpler (b)), plus the reference tile head (each fine tile's frame 11 and change since the reference frame, box-supervised); v2's stack configurations with 'tileref' added to those that use the reference; window and fog heads selected as before (now on the dev sets plus hpwren_bg); zoom crops still chosen by the v1 tile head (stored as the detector's zoom selector). Also compared on dev and not adopted (no gain beyond noise): a wider tile-head C grid (0.01, 0.03; never chosen), four leaner stack designs (0.864-0.868 vs 0.865 without hpwren_bg).

Dev out-of-fold (v3dev experiment, window head fixed at v2's selection, dev sets plus hpwren_bg, deploy at 80 % dev recall): (a) v2 recipe + hpwren_bg: within-set smoke AUROC 0.837, FIgLib 0.796, alarms on dev fog 1.9 %, on all smoke-free 15.2 %, on FIgLib pre-ignition 55 %, on background 9 %; (d) chosen: 0.870, 0.832, 1.2 %, 9.5 %, 34 %, 6 %. The dev numbers of the chosen variant are optimistic by the selection among about ten variants.

Box rule fixed after an independent code review, before the dev comparison above: a box spread over several tiles, none holding a quarter of it, labels the tiles holding most of it (it had left such windows unlabelled; 4 of 401 medium/high-confidence boxes).

2026-10-20, after the fresh-test scoring, a description correction only: the dev background windows had been selected with a 70 km / 7 day incident exclusion (recorded per window in data/real/hpwren_bg/candidates.csv), not the 100 km / 14 days this file first stated; the selection itself, the data and every result are unchanged. Found by an independent check of the write-up.
